source.states: ReceiptEdit US State Sales Tax Dataset 2026.1 (https://github.com/receiptedit/us-sales-tax-2026), last updated 2026-06-17, MIT. District of Columbia 6.00% statewide rate from the DC Office of Tax and Revenue.
source.zips: DeepCalc US sales-tax ZIP table (https://deepcalc.com/data/us-sales-tax/zip), dominant combined rate; primarily 2026 Q3 (Ohio 2026 Q1, Iowa 2025 Q3, Nevada 2025 Q4). Only ZIPs that differ from the state base rate are stored.
source.prefixes: USPS ZIP Code prefixes via alecperkins/zip-state (CC0). Prefixes 202-205 are mapped to DC (USPS unique/government ZIPs).
source.vehicle: Official state DMV/DOR pages and statutes, corroborated by the Pennsylvania DOR Sales and Use Tax Credit Chart (REV-227, updated 2026-09-12). These are motor-vehicle titling/excise/highway-use rates, not general retail sales-tax rates. Vehicle-rate table as of 2026-11.
source.localZips: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance, Publication 718 (2/25), effective March 1, 2025, combined state+local rates by county; ZIP-to-county from Census 2020 ZCTA-to-county relationship (largest land-area overlap). Yonkers ZIPs 10701-10705 and 10710 use the Yonkers 8.875% city rate. Unique/firm ZIPs in NYC borough prefixes 100-104, 111-114, and 116 that are not ZCTAs are filled at the NYC 8.875% rate. Pennsylvania Department of Revenue: 6% state motor vehicle sales tax, plus 2% local for vehicles registered in Philadelphia and 1% in Allegheny County. ZIP-to-county from Census 2020 ZCTA-to-county relationship; all mapped PA ZIPs are stored (6% outside Philadelphia and Allegheny).

notes.text: Alabama taxes motor vehicles at a 2% state rate (general sales tax is 4%); local rates still apply. Estimated as the combined general rate minus 2 percentage points.
Delaware has no sales tax. The DMV document fee is 5.25% of purchase price (effective October 1, 2025).

DC excise tax is 1%–11% of fair market value by unladen weight and city MPG (electric vehicles 1%–3%), effective February 17, 2025. 6.00% is a mid-range estimate (3,500–4,999 lb, 21–25 MPG). Enter the rate for this vehicle.
Florida state rate is 6%. County discretionary sales surtax applies only to the first $5,000 and is not included in this estimate (at most about $75).
Georgia charges a 7% Title Ad Valorem Tax (TAVT) in place of sales tax. No local sales tax on the title.
Iowa exempts motor vehicles from sales tax and charges a 5% fee for new registration.
Indiana charges a 7% statewide rate on motor vehicles; local sales tax does not apply.
Kentucky charges a 6% motor vehicle usage tax statewide; local sales tax does not apply.
Maryland charges a 6.5% vehicle titling excise tax (general sales tax is 6% and does not apply).
Minnesota motor vehicle sales tax is 6.875%. Local sales tax does not apply. A few cities levy a separate local vehicle excise tax that is not included.
Some Minnesota cities levy a separate local vehicle excise tax that is not included in this estimate.
Mississippi taxes motor vehicles and light trucks (10,000 lbs or less) at 5% (general sales tax is 7%).
Different rates apply to heavier trucks and some other vehicles; not modeled.
North Carolina charges a 3% highway use tax in place of sales tax.
A $2,000 cap applies only to Class A/B commercial motor vehicles and recreational vehicles, not to typical cars, SUVs, or light trucks.
North Dakota charges a 5% motor vehicle excise tax in place of sales tax.
New Mexico charges a 4% motor vehicle excise tax (not the gross receipts tax).

OK.name: motor vehicle excise and sales tax

notes.text: Oklahoma charges 3.25% motor vehicle excise tax plus 1.25% sales tax (4.50% combined). Local sales tax does not apply.
South Carolina charges a 5% infrastructure maintenance fee in place of sales tax, capped at $500.
South Dakota charges a 4% motor vehicle excise tax (general sales tax is 4.2%).
Texas charges a 6.25% motor vehicle sales tax. Local sales tax does not apply to motor vehicles.
Vermont charges a 6% purchase and use tax on automobiles and light trucks.
A $2,486 cap applies to heavy trucks (curb weight 10,100 lbs or more) and some other vehicles, not typical cars or light trucks.
West Virginia charges a 6% statewide titling sales tax. Local sales tax does not apply.
A flat $30 titling tax applies when the net purchase price is under $500; not modeled.
Connecticut charges the 6.35% state rate on motor vehicles; there is no local sales tax.
A 7.75% rate may apply to vehicles priced over $50,000; not modeled. Enter the rate by hand if it applies.
Alaska has no state sales tax. Some boroughs and cities tax vehicle purchases locally. If no ZIP rate is on file, the quote uses 0% and notes that local tax may apply.
Arizona charges a 5.6% state transaction privilege tax plus local rates on motor vehicle purchases.
Arkansas charges 6.5% state sales tax plus local rates on motor vehicles, generally collected at registration.

California charges a 7.25% statewide sales and use tax plus district taxes on vehicles registered in a district. If no ZIP-level combined rate is on file, the quote uses 7.25% and notes that local tax may apply.
Colorado charges 2.9% state sales tax plus state-administered local taxes on motor vehicles, generally based on where the vehicle will be registered.
Hawaii GET is 4% plus a 0.5% county surcharge in all four counties, so vehicle sales are estimated at 4.50%. Dealers may pass on up to 4.712%.
Idaho charges a 6% state sales tax on motor vehicles. A few local resort or auditorium taxes may also apply.

Illinois dealer sales of motor vehicles are subject to the 6.25% state rate plus local retailers occupation taxes where they apply. If no ZIP-level rate is on file, the quote uses 6.25% and notes that local tax may apply.
Kansas charges 6.5% state sales tax plus local rates on motor vehicles.

Louisiana state sales tax is 5% as of January 1, 2025 (it had been 4.45%). Local parish and city taxes also apply to motor vehicles. If no ZIP-level combined rate is on file, the quote uses 5% and notes that local tax may apply.
Missouri charges 4.225% state sales tax plus local rates on motor vehicles, generally collected at the license office.
Nebraska charges 5.5% state sales tax plus local rates on motor vehicles.
Nevada charges 6.85% state sales tax plus local rates on motor vehicles.

New York charges 4% state sales tax plus county and city local tax (and 0.375% MCTD tax in the downstate district) on motor vehicles, at the combined rate of the owner's resident jurisdiction. ZIP-level rates follow Publication 718 county/city rates mapped from Census ZCTA to county; ZIP boundaries may not match tax jurisdictions exactly.
Ohio charges 5.75% state sales tax plus county and transit rates on motor vehicles.
Pennsylvania charges 6% state sales tax on motor vehicles, plus 2% local tax if the vehicle is registered in Philadelphia and 1% if registered in Allegheny County.

Tennessee charges 7% state sales tax on the full vehicle price. Local option tax applies only to the first $1,600 (the cap is lower in a few counties), and an additional 2.75% state single-article tax applies from $1,600.01 through $3,200. Those extras are not included (together they are typically under $100).

Utah state sales tax is 4.85%. Local option taxes also apply to motor vehicles (some special resort or correctional-facility taxes do not). If no ZIP-level combined rate is on file, the quote uses 4.85% and notes that local tax may apply.
Washington charges 6.5% state sales/use tax plus local rates on motor vehicles, generally at the rate where the vehicle will be registered.
Wisconsin charges a 5% state sales tax plus county and stadium district taxes on motor vehicles where those taxes apply.
Wyoming charges 4% state sales tax plus local option taxes on motor vehicles.
